u-dui-1-24in.summary: 1st Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment, nicknamed "Deuce Four". The 24th Infantry Regiment was organized on 1 November 1869 as a Black regiment (Buffalo Soldiers); the battalion was reactivated on 24 August 1995. The picture is the 24th Infantry Regiment's distinctive unit insignia: a blockhouse on a blue disc with the scroll "San Juan".
facts: Regiment organized 1 November 1869 from the 38th and 41st Infantry Regiments; its enlisted Soldiers were all Black.
1898: assaulted the Spanish-held blockhouse and trenches on San Juan Hill, Cuba. The insignia's blockhouse and "San Juan" scroll refer to this.
1916: Mexican border, then General Pershing's Punitive Expedition. World War II: South Pacific from April 1942, including Guadalcanal.
Korean War: deployed June 1950 and earned the Republic of Korea Presidential Unit Citation for the Pusan defense. Inactivated 1 October 1951.
Reactivated 24 August 1995 in the 1st Brigade, 25th Infantry Division. Iraq 2007-08 (Diyala, Meritorious Unit Citation); Afghanistan 2011-12 (Zabul).
Deuce4.com, a veteran-led site that says it is not an official Army site, describes today's identity as the "Arctic Legion", with Soldiers serving in Alaska, and honors the Iraq-era "Punishers".
Not shown: the Deuce4.com crest. That image is copyrighted by the site, so it is not used here. The picture is the public-domain regiment insignia.
sources: Deuce4.com, "A Living Legacy" (https://deuce4.com/a-living-legacy/), a veteran-led initiative, not an official Army site
